 Elections How Trump may affect Election Day (and how he already has)
 Georgia has been central to the president’s claims of rigged elections and threats of federal intervention. Share President Donald Trump speaks during a midterm campaign rally at Guardian Centers in Perry on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. The Trump administration has taken numerous steps that critics say amount to election interference. (Hyosub Shin/AJC) By David Wickert 3 hours ago President Donald Trump’s administration has turned to criminal investigations, lawsuits and other actions that critics say amount to an unprecedented effort to use the power of the federal government to influence an election.
 Courts have largely rejected those efforts, and many election experts doubt they will be successful. But they’re watching nonetheless.
 Related Story ‘The Final Tally,’ a 3-part podcast on election integrity, debuts October 30, 2026 “I think we have to expect, if the election doesn’t go the way the president wants, that we will see the administration attempt to sow doubts in the election and maybe even challenge those results,” said David Becker, executive director of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, an organization that works with election officials to build voter confidence.
